singularLabel: Jupiter's equatorial diameter
assumption: Jupiter's equatorial diameter is about 142,984 km, converted to metres; NASA labels the planetary dimensions approximate.
sourceNote: NASA planetary guide gives Jupiter's equatorial diameter as about 142,984 km.

singularLabel: Neptune's average distance from the Sun
assumption: Neptune's average distance from the Sun is about 4.5 billion km, converted to metres; this is an orbital average.
sourceNote: NASA gives Neptune's average solar distance as 4.5 billion km.

singularLabel: Jupiter's orbital period
assumption: NASA's approximate 11.9 Earth-year Jupiter orbit is expressed as 375,535,440 s using 365.25 days per year.
sourceNote: NASA's Jovian data table lists Jupiter's orbit period as 11.9 Earth years.

referenceLabel: light travel times from the Sun to Neptune
singularLabel: light's approximate travel time from the Sun to Neptune
assumption: NASA lists 4.2 light-hours from the Sun to Neptune; 4.2 h is 15,120 s.
sourceNote: NASA's Jovian data table lists Neptune at 4.2 light-hours from the Sun.

singularLabel: an official volleyball court's length
assumption: An official volleyball court is 18 m long, measured as the playing court rather than its safety run-off.
sourceNote: Volleyball England states an official court is 18 m by 9 m.

singularLabel: an official volleyball court playing area
assumption: An 18 m by 9 m official volleyball court has a 162 m² playing area; run-off is excluded.
sourceNote: Volleyball England gives 18 m by 9 m; area is exact multiplication.

referenceLabel: built LEGO Eiffel Tower model heights
singularLabel: a built LEGO Eiffel Tower model
assumption: LEGO set 10307 is approximately 149 cm high when built: 1.49 m. This is model height, not the real tower or a physical precision specification.
sourceNote: LEGO gives the set's built height as 149 cm.

referenceLabel: pairs of AirPods 5 earbuds without a case
singularLabel: a pair of AirPods 5 earbuds without a case
assumption: Apple lists each AirPods 5 earbud at 4.3 g. Two earbuds therefore have a nominal combined mass of 8.6 g (0.0086 kg), excluding any charging case.
sourceNote: Size and Weight (Each): 4.3 g per earbud. The separate 32.3 g figure belongs to the USB-C charging case, not the earbuds.

singularLabel: a Nintendo Switch 2 sleep-mode charging time
assumption: Nintendo estimates about 3 hours to charge in sleep mode; this is 10,800 s and is an approximate product charge time.
sourceNote: Nintendo lists approximately 3 hours charging time in sleep mode.

singularLabel: a Joy-Con 2 controller battery runtime
assumption: Nintendo estimates approximately 20 hours (72,000 s) for Joy-Con 2 battery life. This is a nominal comparison; actual duration varies with usage.
sourceNote: Nintendo lists approximately 20 hours for Joy-Con 2 battery life.

referenceLabel: AirPods 5 wireless charging cases without earbuds
singularLabel: an AirPods 5 wireless charging case without earbuds
assumption: Apple lists the wireless charging-case variant at 34.7 g (0.0347 kg). This is the case alone, not the earbuds plus case; the USB-C-only case is a different 32.3 g variant.
sourceNote: Charging-case dimension block lists 32.3 g for USB-C-only and 34.7 g for wireless variant; each earbud is separately 4.3 g.

singularLabel: a left Joy-Con 2 controller
assumption: Nintendo’s Singapore specification lists approximately 66 g (0.066 kg) for the left Joy-Con 2 with a non-removable internal battery. Console and strap are excluded; other regional battery variants can differ.
sourceNote: Nintendo's specifications list the left Joy-Con 2 at approximately 66 g.

singularLabel: Jupiter
assumption: Use NASA’s approximate 317.8 Earth masses and its Earth value 5.97219e24 kg: 1.897961982e27 kg. This is an approximate planetary mass, not a rigid object for standard-gravity lift scenes.
sourceNote: Jovian table: 317.8 Earth masses. Earth mass: https://science.nasa.gov/moon/by-the-numbers/. Product computed in code; source precision remains approximate.

singularLabel: a USPS Love 2024 stamp pane
assumption: Use the entire USPS Love 2024 pane of 20 stamps, including its margins: 140.970 by 146.304 mm gives 0.02062447488 m². This is the pane footprint, not the sum of stamp areas.
sourceNote: USPS lists the full pane as 5.5500 by 5.7600 inches / 140.970 by 146.304 mm.

singularLabel: a standard 22-yard cricket pitch length
assumption: Use the ICC men’s ODI standard pitch length of 22 yards: 20.1168 m by exact yard conversion. The source’s 20.12 m is rounded; this is the pitch, not the whole cricket ground.
sourceNote: ICC states 22 yards/20.12 m length.

singularLabel: a standard cricket pitch rectangle
assumption: Use a standard ICC men’s ODI 22-yard by 10-foot pitch rectangle: 20.1168 m × 3.048 m = 61.3160064 m². Exclude the outfield. This is the nominal rectangle; the source allows a side-boundary exception beside an adjoining artificial pitch.
sourceNote: ICC supplies both dimensions; area is calculated.

singularLabel: a standard 250-metre championship velodrome lap
assumption: UCI says 250 m tracks are most common and standard for World Championships and Olympic Games.
sourceNote: UCI identifies 250 m as the common championship track length.

singularLabel: the Shanghai velodrome’s maximum bank angle
assumption: Use the Shanghai velodrome’s published maximum bank angle of 45 degrees on its bends. This is a named venue maximum, not the angle of its straight sections or a universal velodrome angle.
sourceNote: UCI lists maximum bend incline as 45 degrees.

referenceLabel: 2025 World Rowing maximum eights-boat section lengths
singularLabel: the 2025 World Rowing maximum length of one eights-boat section
assumption: The March 2025 World Rowing rules cap each section of a boat used in eights events at 11.9 m and require at least two sections. This is a named rule limit for a section, not the length of a whole boat or a typical manufactured section.
sourceNote: World Rowing gives 11.9 m maximum section length.

referenceLabel: the stated 30 mph built-up-road limit in England, Scotland and Northern Ireland
singularLabel: the stated 30 mph built-up-road limit in England, Scotland and Northern Ireland
assumption: Use the named 30 mph reference in GOV.UK’s built-up-road table for England, Scotland and Northern Ireland: 13.4112 m/s. Wales has a different default, and signs can set other limits. This compares speed magnitudes; it is not driving guidance.
sourceNote: GOV.UK lists the 30 mph / 48 km/h built-up-area limit.

referenceLabel: the stated 70 mph motorway limit for cars without trailers
singularLabel: the stated 70 mph motorway limit for cars without trailers
assumption: Use GOV.UK’s stated 70 mph motorway limit for cars without trailers as a named speed reference: 31.2928 m/s. Local signs and conditions can require lower speeds. This is a magnitude comparison, not driving guidance.
sourceNote: GOV.UK lists 70 mph / 112 km/h.

referenceLabel: roughly 35-minute driving portions of a DVSA car test
singularLabel: the roughly 35-minute driving portion of a DVSA car test
assumption: GOV.UK says the driving portion lasts around 35 minutes: 2,100 seconds. This excludes other parts of the test and is approximate, not the total appointment length.
sourceNote: GOV.UK lists around 35 minutes driving time.

singularLabel: the DVSA new-style number-plate eyesight-check distance
assumption: The GOV.UK car-test description specifies 20 m for its new-style number-plate check. This is a named test distance, not a statement about every jurisdiction or an individual’s vision.
sourceNote: GOV.UK gives 20 m for new-style plates.

singularLabel: a Korg MA-2 metronome with batteries
assumption: Korg lists the MA-2 at 68 g including batteries, expressed as 0.068 kg.
sourceNote: Korg gives 68 g including batteries.

singularLabel: Yosemite Falls’ total height
assumption: USGS describes Yosemite Falls as approximately 739 m high. Use this named waterfall’s total height; do not label it one uninterrupted vertical drop.
sourceNote: USGS gives approximately 739 m.

singularLabel: the Natural History Museum taxidermy giraffe’s height
assumption: The museum says its taxidermy giraffe is 4.35 m from hoof to horn; this is a specimen measurement, not a species average.
sourceNote: Natural History Museum gives 4.35 m for the named specimen.

singularLabel: a common house mouse body length
assumption: The Natural History Museum describes the common house mouse (Mus musculus) body as around 10 cm long: 0.1 m. Exclude the tail; this is an approximate profile description, not a measured individual or a universal species constant.
sourceNote: Natural History Museum gives around 10 cm for the body.

referenceLabel: UCI 2026 mass-start road handlebar minimum widths
singularLabel: the UCI 2026 mass-start road handlebar minimum width
assumption: Use UCI’s 400 mm outside-to-outside minimum for mass-start road and cyclo-cross handlebars effective January 2026: 0.4 m. This is a named rule limit, not a typical handlebar width or the separate brake-hood spacing.
sourceNote: Later UCI statement confirms the 400 mm overall minimum for mass-start road/cyclo-cross; the separately revised hood spacing is not used.

singularLabel: the UCI 2026 road-race maximum rim height
assumption: Use the UCI statement’s 65 mm maximum wheel-rim height for road races from January 2026: 0.065 m. This is a named regulation threshold, not a typical rim height or a general limit for all bicycle disciplines.
sourceNote: UCI states a 65 mm maximum rim height.

singularLabel: a one-litre smartwater bottleful
assumption: Coca-Cola’s Canadian package list includes a 1 L smartwater bottle. Count its nominal drink contents: 0.001 m³, not the bottle’s external volume or a claim about every bottle size.
sourceNote: Coca-Cola lists 1 L among smartwater package sizes.
